body:
Three unpublished Worker 1 stock proposals turn a storage or autoclaving atmosphere into an asserted material component:

- `CS-PROP-NBRC361_NEUTRALIZED_SULFIDE_STOCK`: Nitrogen is listed as a component based on autoclaving under N2 and sealed storage.
- `CS-PROP-NBRC1321_SULFIDE_STOCK`: Nitrogen is listed as a component based on storage under N2 after filtration.
- `KG26-PROP-186-IDENTITY` / `DSMZ863_Sodium_Carbonate_Stock`: Carbon dioxide is listed as a component based on autoclaving sealed vessels under CO2.

The captured [NBRC361](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=361), [NBRC1321](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1321) and [DSMZ863](https://www.dsmz.de/microorganisms/medium/pdf/DSMZ_Medium863.pdf) instructions establish those preparation conditions. They do not specify the gas as a material ingredient or provide a dissolved-gas specification for these stocks. `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` section 6 defines `components` as material has-part, not every participant in a preparation procedure.

Retain the atmosphere conditions and exact source provenance in notes/evidence. Remove unsupported gas-component assertions, or supply direct applicable evidence for material inclusion. Recheck component completeness against the source's actual material inputs. Do not invent gas amounts or final dissolved speciation.

Keep the explicit CO2 saturation of the separate bicarbonate preparations distinct: there the source does describe introducing CO2 into the solution, without establishing a numerical concentration. This finding does not remove that sourced distinction or merge any owners.

Independent finding: `.temp/all-unmatched-20261107/preflight/w01-shard-coordinator-review-v2/finding-004-atmosphere-partonomy.json`, SHA256 `34b1123989cef7421dc05cf926f2001c18d0fac12a43463da83eabba8dc48d71`. It binds exact frozen payloads, source captures and case IDs. A coordinator check of the current proposals still found all three gas components. Current issue deduplication and the worker's artifact-finding/issue-plan files showed no existing tracker for this specific defect.

Correct only proposal artifacts through the guarded writer, preserve earlier versions and obtain independent re-review. No maintained data, scientific hold or release disposition has changed for this finding.
title: Keep storage and autoclave atmospheres out of unsupported stock material components

Found in the second review of PR #881 (head 54e09be6).

These names are on records #881 already edits. Each resolves, through `docs/data/label_index.csv`, to a form or substance its text contradicts. #878's list missed them because they don't parse as hydrate counts.

| name | on record (identity) | resolves to | should be | CultureMech rows |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| `MgSO .7H O` | `Magnesium_Sulfate` (CHEBI:32599, anhydrous), EXACT_SYNONYM | anhydrous MgSO4 | the heptahydrate CHEBI:31795 (subscripts lost) | 17 |
| `Glauber's salt`, `Glaubersalz` | `Na2so4` (CHEBI:32149, anhydrous), RAW_TEXT | anhydrous Na2SO4 | the decahydrate CHEBI:32586 (ChEBI lists both there) | 0 |
| `magnesium dichloride--water (1/2)` | `Magnesium_Chloride` (CHEBI:86345, hexahydrate), RAW_TEXT | the hexahydrate | the dihydrate CHEBI:131394 | 0 |
| `Natriumsulfid` | `Na2so3` (CHEBI:86477, sulfite), EXACT_SYNONYM | sodium sulfite | sodium **sulfide** (German) | 0 |

`MgSO .7H O` is the one with reach.
- Its 17 recipes are CCAP media (CultureMech:000044–000310).
- Their own `term.id` is CHEBI:31795, but CultureMech replaces it with MIM's trusted answer, CHEBI:32599. `mappings/culturemech_recipe_membership.tsv` therefore counts all 17 under the anhydrous record.
- The unified-mapping side is #868; the label-index side is #811.

**Fix in #881:**
- **Move to the matching record:** `MgSO .7H O` to `Mgso4_X_7_H2o`, with an override and a scoped membership correction; the Glauber names to `Na2so4_X_10_H2o`. All four records are already WITHHOLD.
- **Retype to `REJECTED_LABEL` only:** `magnesium dichloride--water (1/2)` and `Natriumsulfid`. Their correct records (`Mgcl2_X_2_H2o`, `Na2s`) are SUPPORTED, and adding a synonym there would cancel those approvals (#898). The two relocations are tracked in #900.

**Not fixed here:** the rest of the damaged-subscript family (`CaCl .6H O`, `ZnCl .6H O`, `EDTA.Na .2H O` and others) is on records #881 does not touch. It goes to #811.
title: Wrong-form names on records #881 edits: MgSO .7H O (17 recipes), Glauber's salt, magnesium dichloride--water (1/2), Natriumsulfid

body:
Found during the adversarial review of #366. **Pre-existing — not introduced by that PR**, which merely surfaced it by recording `CHEBI:26833` as a component.

MIM has three live records for what a recipe calls sulfur, on three different things:

| record | identifier | what ChEBI says it is |
|---|---|---|
| `Sulfur` | `CHEBI:26833` | **sulfur atom** — formula `S` |
| `Sulphur` | `CHEBI:17909` | **polysulfur** |
| `Sulfur (powder)` | `kgmicrobe.compound:sulfur_powder` | minted in #338 |

## The problem

**`CHEBI:26833` is an atom, not a substance.** Its formula is a bare `S`. Nothing is weighed into a medium as sulfur atoms; what goes in is elemental sulfur, S₈ — `CHEBI:33403 elemental sulfur`. This is the same class-vs-substance error as the structureless-class work in #322, one level further down: an atom is not even a class of substances, it is a constituent of one.

`Sulphur` → `CHEBI:17909 polysulfur` is closer but still a class (chains of variable length), and `Sulfur`/`Sulphur` are simply the US and UK spellings of one word, so having them on two different terms is a spelling artefact with semantic consequences.

## Where it propagates

`label_index.csv` publishes both spellings, so a consumer joining on either gets a different answer:

    Sulfur   preferred_term  CHEBI:26833   (sulfur atom)
    Sulfur   synonym         CHEBI:17909   (polysulfur, via Sulphur)
    sulfur   synonym         CHEBI:26833

And #366 recorded `CHEBI:26833:sulfur` as a component of `Yeast Extract + Sulfur`, faithfully mirroring the `Sulfur` record — so the atom now appears in a decomposition too.

## Suggested resolution

Consolidate onto `CHEBI:33403 elemental sulfur` for the weighable substance and merge the spelling variants, keeping `Sulphur` as a synonym. `Sulfur (powder)` was minted in #338 because its CAS was hydrogen sulfide (withdrawn there); with the family consolidated it may no longer need its own mint.

Worth checking the same pattern for other elements — a quick scan for records whose ChEBI label ends in " atom" would show whether this is one record or a family.
title: The sulfur family is three records on three different notions of sulfur
